chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The pilgrim (for Hajj) and the pilgrim (for Umrah) are under the Guarantee of Allah. So if he dies while heading (for the pilgrimage), Allah will forgive his sins; and if he dies in Ihram, Allah will resurrect him reciting the Talbiyyah; and if he dies in one of the two Sanctuaries (Mecca or Medina), Allah will resurrect him among the secure ones; and if he dies on his way back, Allah will forgive him all his sins.

key_terms.الْآمِنِينَ: The secure ones (from fear and punishment)
key_terms.مُحْرِماً: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.مُلَبِّياً: Reciting the Talbiyyah (O Allah, I answer Your call)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for a Muslim who dies while performing Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the concept of 'daman Allah' (Allah's guarantee), where the pilgrim's state of worship acts as a shield against major sins. The four scenarios detail specific eschatological outcomes, highlighting that dying in the state of Ihram or within the holy precincts ensures a resurrection marked by peace and continuous devotion, reflecting the high spiritual station of the pilgrim.
